title: Spin-Resolved Decay of Axion-Like Particles into Electron--Positron Pairs in Strong Electromagnetic Fields
authors: Xiaodan Mao, Yue-Yue Chen, Pei-Lun He
abstract: We investigate spin-resolved decay of an axion-like particle (ALP) into an electron--positron pair in an intense laser field. Using the Baier--Katkov quasiclassical operator formalism and the locally constant field approximation, we derive a compact analytic rate retaining finite ALP-mass effects and the lepton spin degrees of freedom. In the massless limit, the spin-summed rate has the same weak- and strong-field asymptotic scalings as the corresponding photon-induced pair-creation rate, while the pseudoscalar coupling induces distinct spin-resolved channels and spin correlations. A finite ALP mass reorganizes the spectrum across the vacuum threshold, producing purely field-induced pair creation below threshold and spin-dependent oscillatory modulations above threshold through the coherent interplay of vacuum and field-assisted contributions. The entanglement of the produced pair reflects the dominant production mechanism. Near the vacuum threshold in weak fields, the pair is nearly maximally entangled and singlet-like. Away from threshold, the reduced spin state becomes triplet-like, retaining a concurrence of \(1/2\) when strong-field production dominates but becoming separable when vacuum decay dominates. These results identify spin-resolved spectra and entanglement as signatures of finite-mass and threshold effects in strong-field ALP searches.
summary: This theoretical paper calculates the decay rate of an Axion-Like Particle into electron-positron pairs within intense laser fields. By analyzing spin correlations and pair entanglement, the authors establish that these observables provide unique fingerprints for detecting finite ALP mass effects near kinematic thresholds. The methodology combines advanced quantum field theory techniques with semiclassical approximations.
main_problem: The study investigates the spin-resolved decay rate of an Axion-Like Particle (ALP) into an electron--positron pair within the presence of a strong, intense electromagnetic laser field.
main_result: The analysis reveals that spin correlations and entanglement in the produced pair serve as unique signatures distinguishing finite ALP mass effects and threshold physics from standard decay processes. The rate exhibits distinct functional forms depending on whether the process is vacuum-dominated or field-assisted.
method: The authors employ the Baier–Katkov quasiclassical operator formalism, utilizing the locally constant field approximation to derive an analytic expression for the differential decay rate.
model_or_system: The system involves a pseudoscalar coupling interaction between ALPs and leptons ($	ext{a} 	o e^+e^-$) propagating in intense background fields (laser). The analysis covers regimes from massless limits to finite ALP masses, examining spectral reorganization across the vacuum threshold.
key_observables: Spin-resolved decay rate ($	ext{d}\Gamma / 	ext{d}\epsilon_+$), pair entanglement (concurrence), and spin correlations of the produced $e^+e^-$ pair.
important_parameters: ALP mass ($m_a$), electron/positron energies ($\epsilon_\pm$), dimensionless field strength parameters ($\chi_a$), and the threshold parameter $\Delta$.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on the locally constant field approximation (LCFA) and assumes relativistic final states.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the Feynman diagram for the decay, noting that oscillatory structures appear when $m_a > 2m_e$ due to vacuum–field crossover.
paper_structure:
The paper develops the rate calculation using quasiclassical methods, deriving an analytic expression incorporating spin dependence. It then analyzes the behavior across kinematic thresholds ($\Delta=0$), showing a transition from Bessel functions ($K_
u$) in one regime to oscillatory forms ($J_\pm$) in another, unified by Airy functions.
why_interesting: The detailed study of pair production and entanglement signatures in strong fields is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems, as it models particle creation dynamics far from equilibrium using semiclassical methods.
